basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 9.' and it opens '(Vers. 9.) Noe vir justus atque perfectus in generatione sua, Deo placuit. Signanter ait,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 9.) Noe vir justus atque perfectus in generatione sua, Deo placuit. Signanter ait, in generatione sua: ut ostenderet non juxta justitiam consummatam: sed juxta generationis suae justitiam fuisse eum justum. Et hoc est quod in Hebraeo dicitur: Noe vir justus, perfectus erat in generationibus suis: cum Deo ambulabat [Al. ambulat] Noe: hoc est illius vestigia sequebatur.
